design.summary: Fix #3 by (1) making the three shell-embedding builtins (/commit, /commit-push-pr, security-review) actually expand their `!`cmd`` bodies, and (2) covering BOTH surfaces the user touches: the command_api dispatcher AND the ratatui TUI, which bypasses the dispatcher entirely. Reuse the existing SkillShellRunner (rename PromptShellRunner) as the shared host runner, relocated to tool-api so command-api's leaf seam can be injected from every composition root. For the permission gate, the GOAL's "REAL bash-security gate" is the faithful port of claude-code's `hasPermissionsToUseTool(BashTool,{command})` = `permission::PermissionPolicy::authorize_with_mode("Bash", {command}, mode)`, mapping Allow→Allow, Deny→Deny, Ask→Deny. But that real gate REGRESSES the three builtins unless two supporting pieces ship with it, because the port dropped GIT_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS (git is not in read_only_command.rs) and commit-push-pr embeds a non-read-only `gh pr view … || true`. So full 1:1 requires: (a) port the git read-only allowlist into permission/src/read_only_command.rs, and (b) inject each command's own allowed-tools into a per-command-augmented policy before expanding (claude-code's alwaysAllowRules.command injection). This makes it a large, staged change; an allow-all MVP (reuse SkillShellPermissionGate) is the smaller alternative flagged as an explicit human decision.
design.parity_model: claude-code invokes `executeShellCommandsInPrompt` at the COMMAND layer (inside each command's getPromptForCommand / loader wrapper), never in the central processSlashCommand dispatcher. Exactly the prompt-type commands whose body contains `!`…`` / ```!…``` patterns expand: builtins commit.ts:67, commit-push-pr.ts:133, security-review.ts:215, plus the generic markdown loader (loadPluginCommands.ts:378) and skill loader (loadSkillsDir.ts:375). For each extracted command: resolve the shell from frontmatter only (undefined→BashTool; powershell→PowerShellTool iff enabled, else BashTool — never settings.defaultShell), then call the ORCHESTRATOR gate hasPermissionsToUseTool(shellTool,{command},context) which runs rule matching + the bash-safety battery + read-only inference + mode. It is non-interactive and synchronous: anything whose behavior !== 'allow' (BOTH 'ask' and 'deny') throws MalformedCommandError which aborts the WHOLE prompt (patterns are never left in place); on allow the match span is replaced by stdout. CRITICAL: each command first injects its OWN allowed-tools into toolPermissionContext.alwaysAllowRules.command (commit=[git add/status/commit]; commit-push-pr=[git checkout/add/status/push/commit, gh pr create/edit/view]; security-review=frontmatter allowed-tools), and read-only git (git diff HEAD, git branch --show-current, git log) is auto-approved via GIT_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS even when not in allowed-tools. MCP-sourced bodies (loadedFrom==='mcp') NEVER expand. The Rust 1:1 of the gate is permission::PermissionPolicy::authorize_with_mode("Bash", json!({"command":cmd}), mode) → PermissionResult mapped Allow→Allow, Deny{explanation}→Deny{explanation}, Ask{prompt}→Deny{prompt.message}; the existing execute_shell_commands_in_prompt already produces the byte-identical MalformedCommandError text on Deny.
design.builtin_injectmessage_expansion: YES — required for 1:1, with parity evidence. commit.ts is type:'prompt', source:'builtin' (commit.ts:57-64) and its body literally contains `!`git status``/`!`git diff HEAD``/`!`git branch --show-current``/`!`git log --oneline -10`` expanded at commit.ts:67; same for commit-push-pr.ts:133 and security-review.ts:215. In the port these three are commands/core/src/commit.rs:63-66, commit_push_pr.rs:71-75, security_review.rs:28-46 (verified: grep for `!`\`` returns exactly these three), and each returns CommandResult::InjectMessage{content} carrying the RAW `!`git…`` template. Today the dispatcher's InjectMessage arm (dispatcher.rs:369-371) delivers content verbatim as Handled{display} with NO expansion, and the markdown/plugin arm (dispatcher.rs:314-317) only ever wires the UnavailableShellRunner/DenyShellPermissionGate stubs — so no builtin ever expands. The dispatcher must therefore run execute_shell_commands_in_prompt over the InjectMessage content for these commands. NOTE a secondary, separable divergence: builtin InjectMessage→Handled{display} is display-only whereas claude-code prompt commands become the submitted user TURN (Markdown/Plugin already use RunAsTurn at dispatcher.rs:339). Recommendation: expand the content at the InjectMessage arm now (content correctness) but leave the Handled variant unchanged in this task; the user's actual surface is the TUI, which already submits InjectMessage content as a turn (chat_widget.rs:1310→submit_core_prompt). Converting dispatcher InjectMessage→RunAsTurn is a follow-up parity item (see open_questions).
design.tui_coverage: YES — required, and it is the actual surface the user reported. The ratatui TUI does NOT route through command_api::dispatcher (grep finds zero RegistrySlashDispatcher refs under tui/src). /commit typed in the TUI goes chat_widget.rs cmd_commit (1373/1374) → run_core_command (1284) → block_on(handler.handle) (1309) → InjectMessage{content} → submit_core_prompt (1310) → the RAW unexpanded template becomes the turn; chat_widget.rs:1276 explicitly documents that the shell-expansion pass "runs only in the dispatcher." So a dispatcher-only fix leaves the user's TUI /commit broken. The seam: run_core_command already owns a throwaway current-thread runtime and block_on's the handler (chat_widget.rs:1302-1309), so it can run the async expansion in the SAME block_on before submit_core_prompt. Wiring: add an Option<Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>> to ChatWidget (default None = today's verbatim path, keeps every existing ChatWidget::new test unchanged), threaded from run_ratatui off tui_build.runtime exactly like Runtime.bash_runner is threaded today (apps/cli/src/mode.rs:254). In run_core_command's InjectMessage arm, when Some, call command_api::execute_shell_commands_in_prompt(&content, &ctx, &format!("/{name}"), None) inside block_on with the builtin's ALLOWED_TOOLS; on Ok submit the expanded content, on Err surface the error and do NOT submit (mirrors MalformedCommandError aborting the prompt). In-scope for this task, not a follow-up.
design.reuse_strategy: REUSE the existing skill impls, relocated to a shared home (tool-api) so command-api's leaf seam can be injected from every root; do NOT write new runners. (1) RUNNER: move SkillShellRunner (tools/skill/src/skill.rs:211-232 struct + :260-380 run + helpers resolve_skill_shell_path :236-242 and skill_disable_extglob :244-258) into a new tool-api module (e.g. tool_api::prompt_shell) renamed PromptShellRunner. It is already general-purpose — all 7 fields are cloned straight off BuiltinToolContext (skill.rs:834-850) with no skill state — so it is constructible from any &BuiltinToolContext. tool-api is the correct home: it already owns BuiltinToolContext and depends on sandbox+permission+traits+protocol; the only new edge is tool-api→command-api, which is acyclic (command-api deps are only protocol/traits/hooks). (2) GATE: do NOT reuse the allow-all SkillShellPermissionGate (skill.rs:391-401) if pursuing the GOAL's real gate — replace it with a PolicyShellPermissionGate in tool-api that holds the command's effective PermissionPolicy and calls policy.authorize_with_mode("Bash"|"PowerShell", json!({"command":cmd}), mode), mapping Ask→Deny. Do NOT back it with the async traits::permission_gate::PermissionGate (permission_gate.rs:205, returns a different type) and do NOT route through PolicyPermissionGate (policy_gate.rs) which delegates Bash's Ask to an interactive prompt — the expansion path must locally collapse Ask→Deny. (3) Because the gate is per-command (needs that command's allowed-tools baked in), expose a factory trait ShellExpansionProvider in command-api and a concrete PromptShellExpansionProvider in tool-api that closes over BuiltinToolContext + Arc<PermissionPolicy> + mode and builds runner+gate per command. Dependency direction: command-api holds only the Arc<dyn> trait seams; the concrete runner/gate/provider live in tool-api and are constructed at each composition root from the live BuiltinToolContext + Arc<PermissionPolicy>. To unify all three surfaces (skill, dispatcher, TUI) on ONE real gate, add permission_policy: Arc<PermissionPolicy> to BuiltinToolContext (both roots already build it: desktop lib.rs:3517, mobile host.rs:762) — then skill.rs:834-850 also switches to the shared provider.

file_changes.change: Add `pub trait ShellExpansionProvider: Send + Sync { fn build(&self, allowed_tools: &[String], shell: Option<FrontmatterShell>) -> ShellExpansionCtx; }`. Keep ShellExpansionCtx/ShellRunner/ShellPermissionGate as-is (already the 1:1 seams).

Add field `shell_expansion: Option<Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>>` to RegistrySlashDispatcher (near expansion_hooks:111), None in new() (:117). Add `pub fn with_shell_expansion(mut self, p: Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>) -> Self` mirroring with_expansion_hooks (:132). At the Markdown/Plugin arm (:314-317) use `provider.build(cmd.allowed_tools, shell)` when Some, else KEEP the UnavailableShellRunner/DenyShellPermissionGate stubs (byte-identical default). Add the MCP carve-out: skip expansion when command.source==CommandSource::Mcp (loadSkillsDir.ts:371-374). At the InjectMessage arm (:369) when Some AND the command carries embedded patterns, run execute_shell_commands_in_prompt over content with the command's ALLOWED_TOOLS+shell=None before returning Handled{display} (leave the result variant unchanged this task).

Expose per-command allowed_tools for builtins so the dispatcher can pass them into provider.build. Markdown/Plugin already parse frontmatter allowed-tools; add the same field to builtin prompt entries (commit/commit_push_pr/security_review) so their hardcoded ALLOWED_TOOLS reach the gate.

Add `pub permission_policy: Arc<permission::PermissionPolicy>` to BuiltinToolContext so the runner+gate provider is buildable from ctx alone (unifies skill+dispatcher+TUI). Update every construction site (cargo check --workspace — struct-literal breakage is expected per memory).

Relocate SkillShellRunner→PromptShellRunner (+resolve_shell_path, disable_extglob helpers) verbatim. Add PolicyShellPermissionGate implementing command_api::ShellPermissionGate: holds the effective Arc<PermissionPolicy> + mode + shell selection, calls authorize_with_mode(tool_name, json!({"command":cmd}), mode), maps Allow→Allow / Deny{explanation}→Deny{explanation} / Ask{prompt}→Deny{Some(prompt.message)}. Add PromptShellExpansionProvider{ ctx: BuiltinToolContext } implementing command_api::ShellExpansionProvider::build(allowed_tools,shell): builds PromptShellRunner from ctx and a per-command policy = base policy rules + parsed allowed_tools rules (via the permission crate's rule parser), selecting tool_name=PowerShell iff shell==PowerShell && enabled else Bash. Add `pub fn build_prompt_shell_provider(ctx:&BuiltinToolContext)->Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>`. Add tool-api→command-api dep in Cargo.toml (verify acyclic).

Port the git slice of GIT_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS: recognize `git` as a base with a read-only subcommand allowlist (diff, log, status, branch, show, remote show, rev-parse, etc.) so git status / git diff HEAD / git branch --show-current / git log --oneline -10 return command_is_read_only==true. Required or the real gate denies /commit's embedded commands (git is currently absent from READONLY_BASE_COMMANDS:61; only standalone `diff` is present at :70). Also cross-check gh read-only handling; commit_push_pr's `gh pr view … || true` is NOT read-only and relies on the allowed-tools injection instead.

Add each command's ALLOWED_TOOLS constant matching claude-code (commit=[Bash(git add:*),Bash(git status:*),Bash(git commit:*)]; commit_push_pr=[git checkout/add/status/push/commit + gh pr create/edit/view]; security_review=frontmatter allowed-tools) and surface it through the command entry so the dispatcher/TUI pass it to provider.build. Needed because commit_push_pr embeds `gh pr view --json number 2>/dev/null || true` which is neither read-only nor auto-safe.

Delete private SkillShellRunner (211-232,260-380) and SkillShellPermissionGate (391-401) + helpers; at :834-850 call tool_api::build_prompt_shell_provider(&self.ctx).build(desc.allowed_tools, desc.shell) then execute_shell_commands_in_prompt. Keep the desc.skip_shell_expansion (MCP) guard.

At :3517 clone the Arc<PermissionPolicy> before it moves into PolicyPermissionGate::new (:3523); store it in tool_ctx.permission_policy (tool_ctx built at :4290). At dispatcher construction (:5127) chain `.with_shell_expansion(tool_api::build_prompt_shell_provider(&tool_ctx))`. Add a Runtime.shell_expansion field (built from the same tool_ctx) for the TUI, sibling to bash_runner (lib.rs:1860).

Pre-move tool_ctx.clone() (tool_ctx moved at :975) carrying permission_policy (built at :762); chain .with_shell_expansion(...) at the dispatcher (:1112). Mobile has sandbox_available=false so expansion runs unsandboxed via ProcessRunner — consistent with mobile's Bash tool (confirm mobile should shell-expand at all; may prefer leaving mobile dispatcher unwired = default None).

Add Runtime.shell_expansion: Option<Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>> (init.rs neighbor of bash_runner:104). In run_ratatui (mode.rs:213) clone it off tui_build.runtime (mirror mode.rs:254) and pass into ChatWidget.

Add Option<Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>> to ChatWidget (near :86), default None in constructors used by tests. In run_core_command's InjectMessage arm (:1310), when Some, run execute_shell_commands_in_prompt(&content, &provider.build(ALLOWED_TOOLS, None), &format!("/{name}"), None) inside the existing block_on (:1309) before submit_core_prompt; on Err display the error and return without submitting. Expose each builtin's ALLOWED_TOOLS to this arm.
No change required — RegistrySlashDispatcher::new(:272) stays a strict no-op (shell_expansion=None). This test is the proof the injection must be Option-gated.

design.wiring_plan: Dispatcher builder API mirrors with_expansion_hooks (dispatcher.rs:132): `pub fn with_shell_expansion(mut self, provider: Arc<dyn ShellExpansionProvider>) -> Self { self.shell_expansion = Some(provider); self }`, stored as Option (None default = today's stubs, strict no-op). The provider is a factory (not a fixed ShellExpansionCtx) because the gate is per-command — it must bake in that command's allowed-tools. Concrete provider = tool_api::PromptShellExpansionProvider closing over BuiltinToolContext (which now carries permission_policy). Injection at the three sites: (1) engine-desktop build (lib.rs, dispatcher at :5127, tool_ctx at :4290, policy Arc at :3517) — clone the policy Arc before it moves into PolicyPermissionGate::new at :3523, put it on tool_ctx, then `.with_shell_expansion(tool_api::build_prompt_shell_provider(&tool_ctx))`; also stash the same provider on Runtime.shell_expansion (sibling of Runtime.bash_runner at lib.rs:1860/4440) for the TUI. (2) engine-mobile build (host.rs:1112) — same, with a pre-move tool_ctx.clone() since tool_ctx moves into the registry at :975; policy Arc from host.rs:762. (3) bridge-server test (router_test.rs:272) — untouched, remains None. TUI leg: Runtime.shell_expansion → mode.rs run_ratatui (:213) clones it off tui_build.runtime exactly like bash_runner (:254) → ChatWidget field → consumed in run_core_command's block_on (chat_widget.rs:1309). All three surfaces (skill tool at skill.rs:834, dispatcher markdown+InjectMessage arms, TUI run_core_command) call the SAME provider so behavior is uniform and 1:1 with promptShellExecution.ts.
test_plan: command-api unit: dispatcher with a fake ShellExpansionProvider expands `!`echo hi`` in a Markdown command to stdout, and a permission-Deny provider yields the byte-exact MalformedCommandError-derived display (guard shell_expansion.rs:204-213 text).

command-api unit: default (no with_shell_expansion) leaves `!`cmd``-bearing Markdown yielding the current 'expansion failed' display and InjectMessage content verbatim — proves strict no-op / no regression (router_test.rs:272 still passes).
command-api unit: builtin InjectMessage arm — CommitHandler content with the 4 embedded git patterns expands (fake runner echoes) and MCP-source command is NOT expanded (carve-out).

permission unit: command_is_read_only true for `git status`, `git diff HEAD`, `git branch --show-current`, `git log --oneline -10`, `git show`, `git diff origin/HEAD...`; false for `git commit -m x`, `git push` — the new git allowlist.

permission unit: PermissionPolicy::authorize_with_mode('Bash',{command:'git status'},Default)==Allow (via read-only), and with injected rule Bash(gh pr view:*): `gh pr view --json number 2>/dev/null || true` ==Allow (rule+`true` read-only), without it ==Ask.

tool-api unit: PolicyShellPermissionGate maps Allow→Allow, Deny→Deny{explanation}, Ask→Deny{prompt.message}; PromptShellExpansionProvider.build(allowed_tools) produces a gate that allows the per-command tools.

integration (real): /commit through the desktop dispatcher in a git repo expands all 4 embedded commands to real git output; /commit-push-pr expands including the `gh pr view` line (with allowed-tools injected).

TUI: run_core_command('commit',…) with a wired provider returns ChatOutcome::Submit whose content contains real `git status` output not the literal `!`git status``; with a Deny provider returns a display error and NO Submit. Reuse the existing core_bridge_block_on test harness (chat_widget.rs:1839).
TUI regression: ChatWidget::new(default None) still returns verbatim content (existing prompt-type InjectMessage test at chat_widget.rs:1852-1917 unchanged).
workspace: cargo check --workspace --tests after adding permission_policy to BuiltinToolContext (struct-literal breakage expected per memory).
parity_risks: ANTI-PARITY TRAP (the central decision): wiring the real PermissionPolicy gate into ONLY the slash/TUI `!cmd` path makes it STRICTER than the port's model-facing BashTool (allow-all stub, bash.rs:988-997) and the current skill gate. This is CORRECT vs claude-code (promptShellExecution.ts calls the orchestrator gate, not the tool's own check) but is an intentional asymmetry — unify by routing BOTH `!cmd` surfaces (skill+slash) through the same real gate and leaving the model-Bash stub as a separate pre-existing gap; do NOT silently make only the dispatcher strict.

REGRESSION RISK if the real gate ships WITHOUT its two supporting pieces: git is absent from read_only_command.rs so `git diff HEAD`/`git branch`/`git log` would return Ask→Deny and BREAK /commit (worse than today's literal); and commit_push_pr's `gh pr view … || true` is neither read-only nor auto-safe so it REQUIRES per-command allowed-tools injection. Both pieces MUST land together or the three builtins fail.

Ask→Deny message fidelity: claude-code's non-allow message is createPermissionRequestMessage(...) text; to be byte-1:1 the gate must render PermissionResult::Ask{prompt.message} rather than a generic placeholder (result.rs:171).

Live permission mode: authorize uses the policy's boot mode; if the session enters plan-mode live, thread the current mode via authorize_with_mode or expansion uses a stale mode (as PolicyPermissionGate does).

Per-command policy augmentation must be per-EXPANSION (fresh effective policy = base rules + that command's allowed-tools), matching claude-code building a fresh toolPermissionContext per call — do not mutate the shared boot policy.

MCP carve-out: the dispatcher markdown arm and the InjectMessage arm must skip expansion for source==Mcp (loadSkillsDir.ts:371-374); the skill path already gates on desc.skip_shell_expansion — keep it.

Shell selection is frontmatter-only (never settings.defaultShell): builtins pass shell=None→Bash; only .md frontmatter selects PowerShell, and only when enabled else fall back to Bash (promptShellExecution.ts:80-83).

Failure aborts the WHOLE prompt (no partial replacement); the TUI must NOT submit on expansion error, and the dispatcher already surfaces the error instead of running — do not leave patterns in place.
BuiltinToolContext field-add breaks workspace struct literals (memory: 'shared-struct field-add breaks workspace literals'); run cargo check --workspace --tests and fix every construction site.

bash-ast feature: bash_ast_security::parse_for_security returns ParseUnavailable past pre-checks (module doc), so authorize falls through to the legacy bash_command_is_safe battery regardless — confirm the dispatcher crate's feature flags match the Bash tool's so behavior is consistent.

Secondary divergence (flagged, not fixed here): dispatcher builtin InjectMessage→Handled{display} is display-only vs claude-code prompt commands becoming the submitted turn — the TUI already submits so the user symptom is fixed; converting dispatcher InjectMessage→RunAsTurn is a follow-up.
open_questions: KEY DECISION — gate strictness. Recommendation: wire the REAL PermissionPolicy-backed gate (the GOAL demands it and it is the faithful port of hasPermissionsToUseTool), and ship the two required supporting pieces (git read-only allowlist in read_only_command.rs + per-command allowed-tools injection). This is 'large'. The smaller alternative is to reuse the allow-all SkillShellPermissionGate for the slash/TUI path (consistent with the skill path and the port's allow-all model-Bash), which fixes the user's literal-`!`git`` symptom in 'moderate' effort but does NOT satisfy 'REAL bash-security gate'. Pick real-gate+supporting-pieces unless a fast, low-risk first cut is preferred — in which case land allow-all now and the real gate as a fast-follow.

Should the skill path (skill.rs:834) also flip from allow-all to the shared real gate? Recommendation: yes, for consistency (both `!cmd` surfaces are the same claude-code function), but it requires skills to inject their frontmatter allowed-tools into the gate too — include it in the shared provider design.

Should dispatcher builtin InjectMessage→RunAsTurn after expansion (so non-TUI hosts actually RUN /commit, matching type:'prompt')? Recommendation: NO in this task (keep Handled{display}, just expand the content); the primary surface (TUI) already submits the expanded content as a turn. Treat the turn-semantics change as a separate parity item.

Should the mobile dispatcher shell-expand at all (sandbox_available=false → unsandboxed ProcessRunner)? Recommendation: wire it for consistency with mobile's Bash tool, but leaving mobile dispatcher unwired (default None) is acceptable if unsandboxed slash-command expansion on mobile is undesirable.

parity_facts: executeShellCommandsInPrompt is invoked at the COMMAND layer (inside each command's getPromptForCommand), never in the central dispatcher processSlashCommand.tsx:869 which only calls command.getPromptForCommand and does no expansion.

Builtin prompt-type commands /commit (commit.ts:67), /commit-push-pr (commit-push-pr.ts:133), and security-review (security-review.ts:215) DO expand embedded shell; the Rust dispatcher currently expands only Markdown|Plugin (dispatcher.rs:309-311) and passes builtin InjectMessage through verbatim (dispatcher.rs:369-370) — this is the parity gap.

The expansion trigger is 'prompt command whose body contains !` or ```! patterns', not 'all builtins'. In the port exactly commit.rs, commit_push_pr.rs, security_review.rs carry such patterns — 1:1 with the reference set.

Each command injects its OWN allowed-tools into toolPermissionContext.alwaysAllowRules.command BEFORE expanding: /commit=[git add,status,commit]; /commit-push-pr=[git checkout/add/status/push/commit, gh pr create/edit/view]; security-review=frontmatter allowed-tools (git diff/status/log/show/remote show, Read/Glob/Grep/LS/Task).

The real permission gate MUST auto-allow read-only commands independent of the command's allowedTools: /commit runs git diff HEAD, git branch, git log which are NOT in its ALLOWED_TOOLS but pass via GIT_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS (readOnlyCommandValidation.ts:107-807). A gate that only honors alwaysAllowRules would fail /commit.
MCP-sourced command/skill bodies must NEVER be expanded (loadSkillsDir.ts:371-374) — preserve this carve-out.
shell param is undefined for builtins (→ BashTool/bash) and comes only from .md frontmatter for markdown/skill/plugin commands (promptShellExecution.ts:64-83).
Expansion failure or permission-denied throws MalformedCommandError and aborts the whole prompt (promptShellExecution.ts:106-113,132-136); patterns are never left in place on failure.
reusable_pieces: command_api::shell_expansion::execute_shell_commands_in_prompt(text, ctx, name, shell) — already a 1:1 port of promptShellExecution.ts; only needs real injected impls (shell_expansion.rs)
SkillShellRunner (tools/skill/src/skill.rs:261) and SkillShellPermissionGate (skill.rs:391) — the existing REAL host runner + gate pattern to relocate/reuse for the dispatcher
ShellExpansionCtx assembly reference at tools/skill/src/skill.rs:834-851
permission/src/bash_ast_security.rs + permission/src/lib.rs — the bash permission oracle the real gate must call (must include read-only-command auto-allow to match GIT_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS behavior)
RegistrySlashDispatcher::with_expansion_hooks builder (dispatcher.rs:132) — mirror it to inject the real ShellExpansionCtx
dispatcher.rs expand_markdown_command/ExpandCtx flow (dispatcher.rs:314-347) — the builtin InjectMessage arm (dispatcher.rs:369) should route through the same expansion before returning

parity_facts: Embedded `!`cmd`` runs the FULL tool permission pipeline via hasPermissionsToUseTool(shellTool,{command},context) — identical to a model-initiated Bash call, including AST subcommand decomposition + allow/deny/ask rules + mode (promptShellExecution.ts:98-104, permissions.ts:1158-1319).

It is NON-INTERACTIVE: the expansion never prompts. Any decision whose behavior !== 'allow' (BOTH 'ask' and 'deny') throws MalformedCommandError (promptShellExecution.ts:106-113). So the Rust gate is a pure synchronous 2-valued rule check with no prompt round-trip.

Map PermissionResult -> ShellPermissionDecision as: Allow->Allow; Deny->Deny; Ask->Deny (ask is not-allow). The Deny message must equal claude-code's permissionResult.message (fallback literal 'Permission denied').
On any Deny, the ENTIRE expansion fails (Rust returns Err(ShellExpansionError::Malformed) at first Deny — shell_expansion.rs:204-213); message format already matches TS byte-for-byte.

Shell selection is frontmatter-only, never settings: shell==Some(PowerShell) && powershell_enabled -> authorize tool_name 'PowerShell', else 'Bash' (promptShellExecution.ts:80-83). The `shell` arg is already threaded into ShellPermissionGate::check.

The REAL gate must call PermissionPolicy::authorize / authorize_with_mode (permission/src/policy.rs:302,322) directly — NOT Tool::check_permissions (allow-all stub, bash.rs:988-997) and NOT PolicyPermissionGate (which delegates Bash's Ask to an interactive prompt — the path we must avoid).
Bash is DenyByDefault (not in defaults_per_tool.rs AllowByDefault set), confirming an Ask for Bash would otherwise route to a prompt; the gate must locally collapse Ask->Deny.
toolUseID passed to the permission check is '' and the assistant message is an empty createAssistantMessage — no real tool_use id is minted for expansion-time checks (promptShellExecution.ts:98-104).
reusable_pieces: permission::PermissionPolicy::authorize(tool_name,&input) and authorize_with_mode(tool_name,&input,mode) — the real rule-based bash permission oracle (permission/src/policy.rs:302,322), returns PermissionResult::{Allow|Deny|Ask}
permission::PermissionResult + PermissionDecisionReason (rendered deny/ask message source) — permission/src/result.rs (re-exported permission/src/lib.rs:92)
permission::shell_command rule-matching helpers used inside authorize: rule_matches_any_subcommand:467, command_fully_allowed:484 (AST subcommand decomposition)
command_api::shell_expansion::{ShellPermissionGate, ShellPermissionDecision, ShellExpansionCtx} seam — already the 1:1 injection point (shell_expansion.rs:63-122)
SkillTool ShellExpansionCtx assembly pattern at tools/skill/src/skill.rs:834-851 (the reference wiring shape to mirror for the dispatcher)
RegistrySlashDispatcher::with_expansion_hooks builder pattern (dispatcher.rs:132) — mirror it to inject a real ShellExpansionCtx factory into the dispatcher
permission::defaults_per_tool tool_default/PromptDefault (Bash = DenyByDefault) — informs why Ask must be locally mapped to Deny

parity_facts: SkillShellPermissionGate::check (skill.rs:393-400) returns ShellPermissionDecision::Allow unconditionally — allow-all, no bash_ast_security call.
This allow-all is 1:1 with the port's BashTool::check_permissions, which is itself allow-all (bash.rs:988-997, reason 'allow-all-gate (M4-02 default)').
TS promptShellExecution.ts:98-104 gates each embedded command on hasPermissionsToUseTool(BashTool,{command},context); the port models this as the injected ShellPermissionGate.

permission/src/bash_ast_security.rs has ZERO consumers outside the permission crate — the real oracle is unwired; wiring it into ONLY the dispatcher gate would be stricter than the skill path and the model Bash tool (anti-parity).

parity_facts: claude-code promptShellExecution.ts:98 calls hasPermissionsToUseTool(shellTool,{command},context) — the ORCHESTRATOR permission fn — before each embedded command; its Rust 1:1 is permission::PermissionPolicy::authorize("Bash", &json!({"command": cmd})) (policy.rs:302), NOT BashTool::check_permissions and NOT bash_command_is_safe directly.

The bash-security oracle is reached only THROUGH authorize's 2c layer PermissionPolicy::shell_bash_safety_ask (policy.rs:1143), which requires tool_name=="Bash" and input=={"command":...} and calls bash_security::bash_command_is_safe(&stripped) per split subcommand (policy.rs:1186-1193).
bash_command_is_safe(command: &str) -> BashSafetyVerdict{Safe|Ask{message}} (bash_security.rs:1630) is pure/sync and takes ONLY the command string — no rules, mode, or cwd.

Result mapping is 3→2: PermissionResult::Allow → ShellPermissionDecision::Allow; PermissionResult::Deny{explanation} → Deny{message:explanation}; PermissionResult::Ask{prompt} → Deny{message:Some(prompt.message)} — because TS treats behavior !== 'allow' (both ask and deny) as a thrown denial (promptShellExecution.ts:106-114).

The check is SYNC and prompt-free: PermissionPolicy::authorize is sync &self->PermissionResult, and command_api::ShellPermissionGate::check is sync — no .await, no interactive prompt. An Ask verdict is folded to Deny, never a UI prompt.
